pages.title: EPF Statutory Wage Ceiling: 2026
pages.description: EPFO's official FAQ records a ₹25,000 monthly wage ceiling from 17 September 2026, revised from ₹15,000; individual payroll application depends on the facts.
pages.intro: This page summarizes the ceiling revision stated in EPFO's September 2026 FAQ. It does not determine whether a particular employee is covered or calculate contributions from an offer's salary breakup.
pages.change: The FAQ says the statutory ceiling rose from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month, effective 17 September 2026.
pages.plainLanguage: Treat ₹25,000 as the ceiling stated in this FAQ, not as a personal deduction estimate. Check the full FAQ and your own payroll records for the facts that apply to you.

pages.title: Gratuity Wage Rules for Fixed-Term Workers
pages.description: Official Ministry of Labour FAQs explain the gratuity wage definition, fixed-term eligibility, effective date, and why CTC alone is not enough.
pages.intro: The Ministry's 2026 FAQs clarify when the revised wage definition applies to gratuity and what the FAQ says about fixed-term employees. They do not replace the full Code, state-specific rules, or an individual eligibility review.
rows: The Ministry says the revised definition of wages applies to gratuity calculations from 21 November 2025
The FAQ says a fixed-term employee is eligible after one year of service under the contract
Use the inclusions and exclusions in section 2(88) of the Code on Social Security, 2020; the FAQ cautions against adding unspecified components
pages.change: The Ministry dates application of the revised wage definition to 21 November 2025, the Codes' implementation date.
pages.plainLanguage: Do not estimate from CTC alone. Ask payroll which wage components and service dates it used, then compare them with the Code and the Ministry's FAQ.

pages.title: Leave Carry-Forward and Encashment Rules
pages.description: The Ministry's March 2026 answers on worker leave carry-forward and encashment, with state-law limits noted.
pages.intro: These are the Ministry of Labour and Employment's answers as of 16 March 2026. The FAQ distinguishes a worker's Code-based rights from potentially more favourable state-law benefits; it is not a universal payroll calculator.
rows: A worker may carry forward up to 30 days; leave applied for but not granted may be carried forward without that limit
The FAQ says a worker is entitled to leave encashment and states no maximum encashment limit under the OSH&WC Code, 2020
Leave above 30 days that was applied for but not granted may be encashed
The Ministry says an employee is entitled to a more favourable state-law benefit where it applies
pages.change: The FAQ published in 2026 explains the Labour Codes implemented on 21 November 2025; check the applicable state law rather than assuming it was displaced.
pages.plainLanguage: Keep the leave ledger, the dated application, the employer's response, and the applicable state rule. Ask HR to identify whether the policy applies to you as a worker under the Code.
